known_rows.raw: Frank Lincoln Wright was a prominent American architect who lived from 1856 to 1932. He was known for his innovative designs and architectural style, which blended elements of classical architecture with modernist techniques. Wright's most famous works include the Lincoln Memorial in Washington D.C., designed in 1922, and the Frank Lloyd Wright House at Stanford University, completed in 1937. His work often incorporated elements such as columns, arches, and domes, creating a distinctive style that influenced architects worldwide.
